key_insight: Plaquette links real hardware noise physics directly to fault-tolerant quantum-computer logical performance, beyond simplified Pauli-error assumptions.
engineering_relevance: It helps quantum hardware teams choose which imperfections to suppress and estimate thresholds, overheads, and error budgets using device-specific noise models.
method: Compiles a single hardware error model from Kraus operators, Hamiltonian-Lindblad dynamics, or reconstructed channels.
Maps that model automatically to multiple simulator types: stabilizer, XPauli for leakage/environment sectors, near-Clifford for coherent errors, or full-state reference simulation.
Supports three showcased platforms: superconducting qubits, neutral atoms, and trapped ions.
evidence_signal: The authors validate XPauli and near-Clifford samplers against full-state simulation and report that they can match within statistical uncertainty, while Pauli twirling can deviate depending on the noise model.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on choosing the right sampler for the underlying error physics; Clifford-only or Pauli-twirled approximations can misestimate performance for leakage, coherent, or non-Pauli noise.
paper_title: Plaquette: A hardware-aware design platform for fault-tolerant quantum computers
